title: Playing like Bunk and Bunk Johnson's travels
summary: Vincent says Richard played much like Bunk and describes Bunk's wandering to California and Chicago and hard times on tour.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Tell him he played like bunk, huh?
So he played a lot like bunk? Yeah, something like bunk under the stars.
He told me he didn't know who bunk was.

So he didn't know who bunk was? No, he wasn't playing at that time. He was kind of young, kind of playing. Been playing around about 15 years. And see, bunk left here, good while. Bunk went up here, and knew I buried him a long time. Then he went out to California, Chicago, and different places like that, you know. He didn't Alexander walk? Yeah, he was over there with me in Alexander. He lost his teeth. I found his teeth twice. The last time he wasn't with me, and I couldn't find him. So the boys weren't trying to put up no money. We had a hard time out of town. Everybody would go, and they'd pick things up, 15 cents, 15 cents, 15 cents. Go from state to state. My friend said, the manager used to credit. He used to take the money and get with the tickets. Catch it.
